findings.who: A filer whose rental building or business land was taken by a government under eminent domain in 2025, or who abandoned business equipment with no buyer. They were paid a condemnation award, or nothing.
findings.why_no: The gate asks whether they 'sell or trade' property. A condemnation is a forced taking, not a sale. An abandonment has no buyer and no trade.
findings.irs_text: i1040sd p. 1: 'Use Form 4797 to report ... 2. The involuntary conversion (other than from casualty or theft) of property used in a trade or business ... 3. The disposition of noncapital assets'
findings.fix: Ask: 'In 2025, did you (or your spouse) sell, trade, give up, abandon, or have taken (for example by condemnation) any real estate or business property?' In help, say that a government taking with an award counts.

findings.who: A filer who sold small business (section 1244) stock or SBIC (section 1242) stock at a loss in 2025, or whose such stock became worthless. Another case is a securities trader with a mark-to-market election.
findings.why_no: Stock is neither 'real estate' nor 'business property' as the help defines them ('used in a business or rented out, such as equipment, a vehicle or a building'). So the answer to the gate is a truthful no.
findings.irs_text: i1040sd p. 1: 'Use Form 4797 to report ... 4. Ordinary loss on the sale, exchange, or worthlessness of small business investment company (section 1242) stock. 5. Ordinary loss on ... small business (section 1244) stock. 6. Ordinary gain or loss on securities ... held in connection with your trading business, if you previously made a mark-to-market election.'
findings.fix: Add a separate gate question asked of everyone: 'Did you sell stock in a small business you helped start, own stock that became worthless, or trade securities as a business under a mark-to-market election?' A yes routes to the Form 4797 refusal.

findings.who: A partner, S corporation shareholder, or trust beneficiary whose Schedule K-1 reports a section 1231 gain or loss. The entity sold business real estate or equipment; the filer personally sold nothing.
findings.why_no: The gate asks whether 'you (or your spouse)' sold or traded. The entity did the selling, so the filer answers no.
findings.irs_text: i1040sd p. 1: 'Use Form 4797 to report ... a. Real property used in your trade or business; b. Depreciable and amortizable tangible property used in your trade or business'
findings.fix: Add to the help: 'Count a sale by a partnership, S corporation, estate or trust shown on a Schedule K-1 you received (for example, a section 1231 gain).' Or gate on any K-1 that shows such an amount.

findings.who: A filer who inherited an installment note from a parent, or received one in a divorce. In 2025 they collected payments on a sale someone else made in an earlier year. A variant is a filer who sold or cancelled their own installment note in 2025.
findings.why_no: The gate says 'any payment for anything you (or your spouse) sold'. The heir or ex-spouse did not sell the property. A filer who disposed of a note may not see that as a payment on the sale.
findings.irs_text: i1040sd p. 6: 'Also, use Form 6252 to report any payment received in 2025 from a sale made in an earlier year that you reported on the installment method.'
findings.fix: Broaden the gate: 'Did you receive in 2025 any payment on a note or contract for property sold by you, your spouse, or someone whose note you inherited or received, or did you sell, give away or cancel such a note?'

findings.who: A filer who traded rental real estate in a like-kind exchange in 2024. The replacement property arrived in 2025, or a related party who received the property disposed of it in 2025.
findings.why_no: The gate asks what they did 'In 2025'. The exchange began, and to the filer happened, in 2024, so they answer no.
findings.irs_text: i1040sd p. 1: 'Use Form 8824 to report like-kind exchanges. A like-kind exchange occurs when you exchange business or investment property for property of a like kind.'
findings.fix: Add: 'Answer Yes too if you received property in 2025 from an exchange begun earlier, or if you made a like-kind exchange with a relative or related business in 2023 or 2024.'

findings.who: A farmer who sold breeding or dairy livestock or cut timber in 2025. Another case is the owner of a geothermal interest who sold it.
findings.why_no: The filer does not see livestock or timber as 'equipment, a vehicle or a building'. The help names only 'oil, gas or mineral', not geothermal.
findings.irs_text: i1040sd p. 1: 'Use Form 4797 to report ... c. Oil, gas, geothermal, or other mineral property; and d. Section 126 property.'
findings.fix: Extend the help's examples: 'including livestock held for breeding, dairy or draft, timber, geothermal interests, and property bought with farm cost-sharing payments.'
